25. Houston Texans CB Derek Stingley Jr.

19. Minnesota Vikings WR Justin Jefferson

18. Kansas City Chiefs QB Patrick Mahomes

17. Indianapolis Colts RB Jonathan Taylor

12. Houston Texans EDGE Will Anderson Jr.

Maye is the first Patriots offensive player to make the NFL Top 100 since 2022 when Mac Jones was ranked No. 85 coming off a solid rookie season.

The Patriots selected Maye with the No. 3 overall pick in the 2024 draft hoping he could be the answer at quarterback they had been searching for since Tom Brady left after the 2019 season.

After an encouraging rookie season, Maye ascended to superstardom in 2025. He led the NFL in completion percentage (72.0) and QBR (77.1), while ranking in the top five in passing yards (4,394) and passing touchdowns (31).

Maye led the Patriots to a 14-3 record, nearly matching their win total from the previous three years combined (16). They won the AFC East for the first time since 2019 and reached the Super Bowl for the 12th time in franchise history.

Expectations are sky high for the Patriots going into this season, particularly with the addition of A.J. Brown as the No. 1 receiver for Maye. It remains to be seen if they can repeat their success from 2025, but their young quarterback is the primary reason for optimism in New England.

Anderson jumped up 34 spots from last year's top 100 when he came in at No. 46.

The ascent for Anderson comes after he was named to the All-Pro first team and finished second in Defensive Player of the Year voting during the 2025 campaign. He set career-highs with 23 quarterback hits, 20 tackles for loss and 12 sacks.

Anderson was tied for fourth in tackles for loss and tied for eighth in sacks.

On a per-play basis, Anderson was one of the most dominant EDGE rushers in the NFL last year. He ranked fourth in ESPN's pass-rush win rate (23 percent) on 270 pass-rush snaps.

In addition to being able to get after the quarterback, Anderson is an excellent run defender. He finished seventh among all EDGE players with a 28 percent run-stop win rate.

Anderson was the only EDGE to rank in the top 10 in both categories.

The Texans had arguably the best defense in the NFL in 2025 and figure to be right up there again in 2026. Anderson is one of the primary driving forces behind that success, making him more than deserving of his high ranking on the top 100 list.

articles.title: Travis Hunter Used 'Top-of-the-Line Software' in Jaguars' Virtual Meeting Room to Prep for 2026
articles.summary: Jacksonville Jaguars cornerback and wide receiver Travis Hunter has heavily utilized virtual reality technology during his preparations for the 2026 NFL regular season.
articles.body:
Jacksonville Jaguars cornerback and wide receiver Travis Hunter has heavily utilized virtual reality technology during his preparations for the 2026 NFL regular season.

Jeff Howe of The Athletic highlighted Hunter's unique methods, writing, "[Jaguars head coach Liam] Coen ordered the construction of a virtual meeting room over the offseason, knocking down a wall and installing top-of-the-line software to aid the team's mental reps. According to those around the Jaguars, Hunter has utilized the room more than anyone, and it's not particularly close. He can walk into the room, listen to the defensive play call, move to his spot within the formation, watch the offense virtually line up and then handle the necessary checks and communication assignments from there."

Selected second overall in the 2025 NFL draft after winning the Heisman Trophy at Colorado, Hunter arrived in Jacksonville with hopes of him being a difference maker on both sides of the ball.

Hunter's rookie campaign was cut short by a knee injury, though, limiting him to only seven games.

He has worked his way back and should be good to go for the start of the regular season, however, as he has been participating heavily in practice for the past few weeks.

Coen has liked what he has seen out of Hunter during the lead up to the Jags' Week 1 game against the Cleveland Browns on Sept. 13, telling Howe, "He's done so much work in the virtual meeting rooms, walkthroughs, [traditional] meeting room. That's been a huge part of his growth and maturation throughout this training camp. He's put in a lot of time and built his body back up in a physical way, especially his upper half. Just getting him playing confident, to really go out and play. He hasn't played football in a long time, so we're really in that ramp-up process."

Although Hunter played 66.7 percent of the offensive snaps compared to 35.9 percent of the defensive snaps last season, all signs point toward him being a bigger contributor at corner than wideout in 2026.

Back in April, NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported that Hunter would primarily be a cornerback and only a part-time wide receiver during his second season:

Coen seemed to confirm as much this week, telling reporters that Hunter is the Jags' "3A, 3B receiver right now." Meanwhile, Hunter is listed as a starting cornerback on the Jaguars' depth chart .

Per Howe, Hunter is "preparing to serve as the team's No. 1 cornerback," although defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile's scheme figures to mostly keep him on one side of the field rather than having him shadow a certain receiver.

articles.title: Penei Sewell, Jalen Carter, Brock Bowers Top NFL Insiders' Poll of Best Players Under 25 Years Old
articles.summary: Detroit Lions offensive tackle Penei Sewell was named the NFL's best player aged 25 or under in an anonymous poll conducted this week.
articles.body:
Detroit Lions offensive tackle Penei Sewell was named the NFL's best player aged 25 or under in an anonymous poll conducted this week.

Mike Jones of The Athletic polled "nearly two dozen NFL coaches, scouts and front-office members" anonymously, and Sewell earned the No. 1 spot. The top five is as follows:

2. Jalen Carter, DT, Philadelphia Eagles

Sewell, 25, was the No. 7 overall pick in the 2021 NFL draft, and he has been every bit as good as expected.

Primarily playing right tackle, Sewell is a four-time Pro Bowler and three-time First Team All-Pro through five NFL seasons, and he could become an even more important piece for the Lions in 2026.

Following the release of longtime left tackle Taylor Decker, Sewell is set to move from right tackle to left tackle in order to protect quarterback Jared Goff's blind side.

Remaining in the trenches, Philadelphia Eagles defensive tackle Jalen Carter came in at No. 2 on the list.

The 25-year-old Carter is a two-time Pro Bowler through three NFL seasons, plus he finished second in NFL Defensive Rookie of the Year voting in 2023, and he won a Super Bowl and was named Second Team All-Pro in 2024.

Despite injuries limiting him to 11 games and finishing with a career-low three sacks last season, Carter landed a four-year, $152 million contract extension last month.

Rounding out the top three is Las Vegas Raiders tight end Brock Bowers, who enjoyed the best rookie season by a tight end in NFL history in 2024.

Bowers' 112 receptions in 2024 were the most ever by a rookie at any position, plus he recorded 1,194 yards and five touchdowns en route to Pro Bowl and First Team All-Pro honors.

Injuries cost the 23-year-old Bowers five games and limited him to 64 grabs for 680 yards and seven touchdowns last season, but if he stays healthy, he should bounce back in 2026 with Kirk Cousins and Fernando Mendoza throwing him the ball.

articles.title: Tyreek Hill's NFL Future Updated by Drew Rosenhaus After Keenan Allen, Stefon Diggs Contracts
articles.summary: As Tyreek Hill continues to work his way back into peak physical condition coming off a knee injury, the star wide receiver is unlikely to sign with a team before the start of the 2026 NFL regular season.
articles.body:
As Tyreek Hill continues to work his way back into peak physical condition coming off a knee injury, the star wide receiver is unlikely to sign with a team before the start of the 2026 NFL regular season.

Appearing on Friday's episode of The Pat McAfee Show , Hill's agent, Drew Rosenhaus, said he doesn't expect Hill to sign before the season in part because he wants to "take his time" and pick "the right team."

One reason Hill wants to be patient is he may not be ready to play for awhile. ESPN's Adam Schefter said earlier in the offseason the eight-time Pro Bowler might be out until midway through the season.

Hill dislocated his knee and tore multiple ligaments , including the ACL, in the Miami Dolphins' win over the New York Jets in Week 4 last season.

Miami released Hill in February as part of a significant roster overhaul under new general manager Jon-Eric Sullivan and head coach Jeff Hafley.

Hill was among several high-profile veteran wide receiver free agents this offseason. Stefon Diggs and Keenan Allen waited most of the summer before finally landing contracts, as did Deebo Samuel.

Diggs agreed to a one-year deal with the Washington Commanders on Aug. 5. Allen didn't sign until Monday when he got a one-year contract from the Indianapolis Colts. Samuel previously reunited with Kyle Shanahan and the San Francisco 49ers.

The typical timeline for recovery from the type of injury Hill suffered is at least nine months.

Hill is 11 months removed from the injury and has posted videos showcasing his rehab. He recently posted a video on his YouTube channel on July 22 in which he is seen running and working out.

There haven't been any teams firmly connected to Hill at this point, though some contenders stand out as needing help at wide receiver.

The Kansas City Chiefs are among those in that group. Hill is very familiar with the organization, having spent his first six NFL seasons with them from 2016 to '21.

Hill ranks fifth all-time in Chiefs history with 6,630 receiving yards and fourth with 56 touchdowns. He made the All-Pro first team three times and won Super Bowl 54 during his time with Kansas City.

Given the injury he is coming off of and being 32 years old, it would be unreasonable to expect Hill to return at the peak of his football ability. He is skilled enough to be a contributor for a good team looking to add more pass-catching help.

articles.title: Bijan Robinson Says He Watches Kyrie Irving, World Cup Star Videos to Improve Game
articles.summary: Perhaps nobody in the NFL uses elite footwork to dance through the defense better than Bijan Robinson, and the Atlanta Falcons running back may have learned some of those skills outside of the gridiron.
articles.body:
Perhaps nobody in the NFL uses elite footwork to dance through the defense better than Bijan Robinson, and the Atlanta Falcons running back may have learned some of those skills outside of the gridiron.

During an appearance on the Schultz Report with NFL insider Jordan Schultz (20-minute mark), Robinson revealed that he watches NBA and soccer highlights when studying some of that movement while mentioning Kyrie Irving and Michael Olise in particular.

"I watch a lot of basketball players and their movement skills," Robinson said after highlighting Irving's 2016 season in particular.

So what does he take from watching Irving?

"One is footwork. Like how he can maneuver in small spaces," Robinson said. "And then two, his body control. Like, he has exceptional body control."

It may not be the first comparison that comes to mind, but it is easy to see the parallels between Irving gliding through defenders and finishing through contact at the rim and Robinson unleashing devastating cutbacks and speed before powering through defenders at the goal line.

That 2016 season stands out, as Irving helped lead the Cleveland Cavaliers to the championship alongside LeBron James and hit one of the most famous shots in NBA history in Game 7 of the Finals to propel the Eastern Conference team to a win over the Golden State Warriors.

As for Olise, Robinson admired "how he moves through the middle" of the defense while dazzling on the field for France.

All Olise did this summer was lead the World Cup with seven assists while helping France reach the semifinals alongside Kylian Mbappé.

Now Robinson will look to help guide the Falcons to a similar stage while studying the footwork of some of his contemporaries in other sports.

articles.title: Best LBs In The NFL: Has Fred Warner Been Dethroned As League's Best Linebacker?
articles.summary: Who is the best linebacker entering the 2026 season? We ranked the 10 best.
articles.body: No player has arguably been better than their peers at their respective position than Fred Warner since the turn of the decade. But as the San Francisco 49ers' star returns from a gruesome ankle injury that ended his 2025 season prematurely, is Warner still the NFL's best linebacker ahead of the 2026 campaign?  We ranked the 10 best linebackers in the league as we prepare for the new year. Warner, a four-time first-team All-Pro, was one of two players to receive first-place votes in our rankings, with the Detroit Lions' Jack Campbell and the Baltimore Ravens' Roquan Smith among those vying for the top spot.  Here's a full look at our top 10 linebackers entering the 2026 season.  10. Devin LloydCarolina Panthers Greg Auman: Can takeaways be what takes Carolina’s defense from bad to good? In defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero’s first year in Charlotte in 2023, the Panthers had an NFL-low 11 takeaways, improving to 17 in 2024 and 21 last year. Lloyd signed a three-year, $42 million deal after a breakout Pro Bowl year with the Jacksonville Jaguars, in which he had five interceptions to help his former team record 31 takeaways, second-most in the NFL.  It’s concerning that Jacksonville let Lloyd walk from the middle of its defense, but he and edge rusher Jaelan Phillips are two high-dollar additions to Carolina’s defense as they try to improve enough to repeat as NFC South champs. Lloyd is 27 and needs to show last year’s splash plays — notably absent his previous two years — can continue as a defensive spark. 9. Nick BoltonKansas City Chiefs Ben Arthur: Bolton has been one of the NFL’s most steady off-ball linebackers since entering the league in 2021, helping the Chiefs win two Super Bowls. The former second-round pick is coming off his second straight season of 100-plus tackles, six pass breakups, an interception and a forced fumble. In 2025, he tied for third in run stops (86) and 10th in hustle stops (15) among linebackers, according to Next Gen Stats.  With Kansas City’s secondary undergoing a makeover this offseason, Bolton will take on a more pronounced role in Steve Spagnuolo’s back-seven as the green dot. Pass coverage is an area for improvement, though. Opposing quarterbacks had a 93.8 passer rating when targeting him in coverage last season, the third time in five seasons he’s allowed a 90-plus passer rating, per NGS.  8. Ernest Jones IVSeattle Seahawks Eric D. Williams: Only 26 years old, Jones has won two Super Bowl rings in six NFL seasons. Since Seattle made a midseason trade for the South Carolina product with the Tennessee Titans in 2024, Jones has been the green-dot playcaller and a leader for one of the best defensive teams in the NFL. Jones finished with a career-high five interceptions (a franchise record for a linebacker) and 126 combined tackles in 2025, earning second-team All-Pro honors for the first time in his NFL career. Jones has finished with at least 100 tackles for four straight seasons. Jones spent his first three seasons in the league with the Los Angeles Rams, setting a single-season franchise record with 145 tackles in 2023, including a career-high 4.5 sacks. 7. Azeez Al-ShaairHouston Texans Arthur: Once in the shadows of Fred Warner and Dre Greenlaw in San Francisco, Al-Shaair has come into his own as a star linebacker the last couple of years. His aggressive play style sets the tone as the green dot of the Texans’ juggernaut defense. In 2025, the former undrafted free agent registered his third 100-tackle season and posted career-highs in interceptions (two) and pass breakups (nine) to make his first Pro Bowl.  Overall, Al-Shaair is one of the league’s best coverage linebackers. Among qualified linebackers last season, he ranked ninth in both tight windows forced rate and coverage EPA and 20th in ballhawk rate, per NGS.  6. Jordyn BrooksMiami Dolphins Auman: Brooks, 28, is the rare Dolphins star the franchise chose to keep this year, locking him up with a three-year, $48 million deal. He earned first-team All-Pro honors last year, leading the NFL with 183 total tackles, but he’s been productive for a while. Over the last five years, he has the third-most tackles in the league, with more tackles for loss (45) than anyone else in the top five. He’s aggressive at the line of scrimmage, with 3.5 sacks and 13 tackles for loss last year, and he’ll need to be as part of a rebuilding Dolphins roster under new head coach Jeff Hafley.  Can the Dolphins win enough games to stay ahead of the Jets and avoid the AFC East cellar? Brooks is a core piece in Miami that’s part of their past and part of their future as well.  5. Zack BaunPhiladelphia Eagles Ralph Vacchiano: It is still absolutely remarkable that the Eagles viewed Baun as little more than a special teams player when they signed him away from New Orleans in 2024, and instead they got a two-time Pro Bowler and one of their best defensive starters. He was one of the best defenders in the league in 2024 and he had almost identical production last season when he had 123 tackles, 3.5 sacks and two interceptions.  Baun's the perfect versatile linebacker for Vic Fangio’s scheme. He’s got the speed to rush the passer and drop back in tight coverage, and he has better instincts than many linebackers in the league. Linebacker hasn’t always been a strength in Philadelphia. But thanks to the 29-year-old Baun, it is now. 4. Carson SchwesingerCleveland Browns Bucky Brooks: The second-year pro quickly established himself as a tackling machine in the middle of the Browns’ defense. Schweisinger’s instincts, range, and awareness as a "see ball, get ball" defender shrink the field for the opponents, leading to fewer explosive plays against the ultra-aggressive unit.  With the youngster also controlling the game as the green dot wearer, the Pro Bowler’s intelligence and communication skills set him apart from others at the position. 3. Jack CampbellDetroit Lions Henry McKenna: Let’s just start with last season when he had 176 tackles, nine tackles for loss, three forced fumbles, five sacks and four pass breakups. Sort of like a quarterback whose rare arm talent allows him to use every blade of grass, Campbell has the athleticism, range and awareness to be a threat in just about every part of the field. There really isn’t a defensive phase where he doesn’t make an impact. I’m not sure Campbell gets the love he deserves, in part because he’s a defensive playmaker and in part because his position is no longer considered "premium." But to that point, it takes a truly special linebacker to justify the draft position of 18th overall, where the Lions got Campbell in 2023. And he has absolutely made that pick worth it. 2. Roquan SmithBaltimore Ravens Williams: One of the most explosive linebackers in the league, Smith can make plays from sideline to sideline and is one of the best tacklers in the NFL. A four-time Pro Bowler and three-time first-team All-Pro, Smith has eclipsed 100 tackles in all eight of his NFL seasons.  But Smith will have to adjust to a new system with defensive-minded head coach Jesse Minter taking over as the team’s head coach. Smith is looking to take the ball away this season after finishing with zero forced fumbles, sacks and interceptions in 2025. 1. Fred WarnerSan Francisco 49ers Brooks: The NFL’s prototype at the position displays a rare combination of size, speed, intelligence, and violence. Warner is a menacing sideline-to-sideline defender who covers ground like a gazelle, but attacks runners and pass catchers like the Lion King tracking his prey.  Given Warner's penchant for producing big plays as a run defender and in coverage, the All-Pro is the "Mike" linebacker that every defensive coordinator would choose as a foundational piece.

articles.title: Fantasy Football 2026 Best Strategy for Each Pick in 12-Team Mock Drafts
articles.summary: The start of the 2026 NFL preseason's second week is a great reminder that the busy drafting weekend on the fantasy football calender is fast approaching.
articles.body:
The start of the 2026 NFL preseason's second week is a great reminder that the busy drafting weekend on the fantasy football calender is fast approaching.

If you haven't nailed down your draft strategy quite yet, time is absolutely of the essence.

Let's act with some urgency, then, and get right into building an early-round blueprint for each pick position in a 12-team mock draft.

The right target at the 1-1 spot will offer superstar upside with a good amount of safety. That feels like the perfect description for Bijan Robinson, who just reeled off 2,298 scrimmage yards with 11 scores and somehow still seems capable of more. With perhaps the best running back on your roster, you should value playmakers at the 2/3 turn, either doubling up on receiver or spending one pick on a star tight end (Trey McBride or Brock Bowers).

This should be a simple decision, as you can just lock in on whichever of Robinson or Jahmyr Gibbs is left on the board. If it's Gibbs (as it would be here), you should plan on adding a second running back in Rounds 2 or 3 (adding a receiver with the other), just in case Detroit's collection of playmakers starts cutting into Gibbs' touchdown tally.

Ja'Marr Chase gets the slight nod over Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Puka Nacua for arguably offering the best blend of ceiling and floor. Chase is probably WR1 if Joe Burrow stays healthy all season, and he would still be an elite option even if Joe Flacco gets forced into action. Target running back in the second round, and you'll be in good shape to take the best player available in the third.

Nacua will be tempting here, but add Smith-Njigba instead. Seattle's passing volume could increase given the club's questions at running back (no Kenneth Walker III and a still-recovering Zach Charbonnet), and JSN doesn't have a ton of competition for targets. Look for any falling values with your next two picks and give serious consideration to making an elite tight end one of them.

Nacua is almost a PPR cheat code as the No. 1 target in the league's most prolific passing attack. He would be awesome to pair with the top running back on the board in Round 2, and if no one has reached at the positions, you could go tight end or even quarterback in Round 3, potentially giving you a top performer at three different positions with your first three picks.

There is arguably a tier drop here, but maybe there isn't if Jonathan Taylor just stays on the field. During the two seasons in which he made 17 appearances (2025 being one of them), he racked up 4,134 scrimmage yards and 40 touchdowns. With some injuries in his past, though, you should double-tap running back with your second pick just to solidify that strength, then aim for a receiver in Round 3.

Amon-Ra St. Brown is your first-round target, and he's a really good one—always a high-level producer, sometimes a truly awesome one. His elevated floor allows for a risk-reward wager in Round 2 (think Nico Collins, A.J. Brown or Malik Nabers). If you like the depth at running back and believe you could get a good one in Round 4, don't rule out a top-shelf quarterback in Round 3.

This might be a coin-flip call between CeeDee Lamb and Justin Jefferson, but those players don't settle the debate. Rather, the quarterbacks do, so take Lamb and bet on Dak Prescott over Kyler Murray. Running back should be your Round 2 priority (De'Von Achane, Omarion Hampton, Chase Brown), and then circle back to receiver for an upside play in Round 3 to account for Lamb's availability issues (five games missed the past two seasons) and erratic touchdown tally (nine scores over the same stretch).

Last season proved Justin Jefferson isn't immune to horrific quarterback play, but he's still a good value play here. Kyler Murray could stabilize the position, and if he does, Jefferson might be the WR1. You'll still want a second receiver among your first three picks to account for the volatility of Minnesota's passing game, but running back is probably your best Round 2 bet.

There are legitimate worries with Christian McCaffrey (a 30-year-old with a long injury history and a 413-touch workload last season), but they've been accounted for this point. Grab CMC, and you might have just taken the top performer in fantasy (if healthy, obviously) with the 10th overall pick. Add a second running back in Round 2 to safeguard against McCaffrey's risks. In Round 3, you might consider tight ends or quarterbacks if you don't love how wide receiver looks.

This feels like a sweet spot for Ashton Jeanty. He overcome a rough ecosystem to deliver 1,321 scrimmage yards and 10 scores as a rookie, and his Las Vegas Raiders have since made major investments to their quarterback room and offensive line. Take the best wide receiver on the board in Round 2, and if Josh Allen makes it to you in Round 3, take him. You'll have legitimate stars at the three most important positions.

With back-to-back picks to open things up, try a double-tap at running back with James Cook III and De'Von Achane. Both were top-7 running backs last season, but they do have some questions (possible touchdown regression for Cook, Miami's offensive infrastructure for Achane). You can mitigate your risks by taking both. A double-tap at receiver at the 3/4 turn is probably your best option, but if Allen slips, he'd be a fun addition.

articles.title: NFL Insiders Explain Where Arch Mannning, Dante Moore Need to Improve Most Ahead of 2027 Draft
articles.summary: Texas quarterback Arch Manning and Oregon quarterback Dante Moore will have to show improvement in a few key areas before the 2027 NFL draft.
articles.body:
Texas quarterback Arch Manning and Oregon quarterback Dante Moore will have to show improvement in a few key areas before the 2027 NFL draft.

For Manning, he'll need to display improved mechanics and become more efficient on shorter throws.

"He has a lot to prove to me this year, but he finished the year strong," an NFC evaluator told ESPN's Jordan Reid . "If he can clean up the lower-body mechanics and underneath accuracy, he has a chance to be the first one picked."

Meanwhile, Moore will have to step up during matchups with top teams.

"He's really good when he's in-rhythm and not under constant duress, but outside of Iowa and Penn State, we just didn't see that enough from him in those big matchups," an NFC director of scouting told Reid. "I'm glad he went back because we'll get another season of tape on him and see him in those high-leverage moments again."

Manning is coming off a 2025 campaign in which he threw for 3,163 yards and 26 touchdowns compared to seven interceptions. Still, he could help the Longhorns' offense sustain drives by connecting on short throws more often.

Among the top 15 passers in the SEC last season, Manning's 61.4 completion percentage represented the third-lowest mark.

Moore helped Oregon finish with a 13-2 record and advance to the College Football Playoff semifinal round during its 2025 campaign, although both of the team's losses came against Indiana.

The 21-year-old struggled when facing the eventual national champions, throwing for 471 yards and three touchdowns while getting picked off three times across two clashes with the Hoosiers.

Expectations are still high for both players, as Manning was projected to be off the board with the No. 3 overall pick in the latest mock draft from Bleacher Report's NFL Scouting Department. Moore was also selected at No. 4.

If they're able to take another step forward during their respective 2026 seasons, they could challenge for the No. 1 spot on the draft board.

articles.title: Texans Sign 2 WRs as NFL Trade Rumors Link Patriots' Boutte, Ravens' Bateman After Higgins Injury
articles.summary: The Houston Texans have signed both Sterling Shepard and Zay Jones after hosting the wide receivers for workouts on Friday, per NFL Network's Mike Garafolo.
articles.body:
The Houston Texans have signed both Sterling Shepard and Zay Jones after hosting the wide receivers for workouts on Friday, per NFL Network's Mike Garafolo.

The news comes after KPRC 2's Aaron Wilson reported that Houston made some "exploratory trade calls" after learning about wide receiver Jayden Higgins' season-ending injury .

The New England Patriots' Kayshon Boutte and Baltimore Ravens' Rashod Bateman were labeled "potential targets" for the Texans prior to Shepard and Jones' contracts, according to Wilson.

Free agent wideout Josh Reynolds was also "on the team's radar," per ESPN's Jeremy Fowler .

Higgins suffered a torn ACL during a joint practice against the Las Vegas Raiders earlier this week, ESPN and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported Wednesday.

Shepard, who spent the first eight years of his career with the New York Giants, spent the last two seasons with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. In 2025, he caught 39 passes for 371 yards and one touchdown in 13 games.

Jones, meanwhile, has played for four different teams throughout his nine-year career--the Buffalo Bills, Las Vegas Raiders, Jacksonville Jaguars and Arizona Cardinals. He spent the last two seasons in Arizona.

In 2025, Jones caught 12 passes for 183 yards in eight games. His best season came in 2022 with Jacksonville, where he caught 82 passes for 823 yards and five scores.

Boutte has been floated as a potential trade candidate since the Patriots acquired A.J. Brown and signed Romeo Doubs this offseason.

Sports Illustrated 's Albert Breer reported in May he felt Boutte could be acquired at the time "for a fifth- or sixth-round draft pick."

Bateman has also been linked to trade possibilities in the past as the Ravens continue turning to Zay Flowers as the team's top wide receiver.

ESPN's Rich Cimini reported in May the New York Jets were considering Bateman alongside three other receivers as trade targets.

However, it's reasonable to think that the Texans are now out on both receivers.

Higgins suffered his season-ending injury after a fall during 11-on-11 drills in the red zone, per ESPN's DJ Bien-Aime .

He was primed to take on a bigger role during his sophomore NFL season after posting 41 catches for 525 receiving yards and six touchdowns in 17 games and 10 starts of the 2025 campaign.

Houston's ability to replace him will be tested by other injuries to the team's wide receiver room. Tank Dell is still working his way back from the knee injury that sidelined him for the entirety of the 2025 season, while Jaylin Noel has been dealing with right pinkie and hamstring injuries .

The Texans have just over a week before the NFL requires teams cut their rosters down to 53 players on Sunday, Aug. 30.

articles.title: De'Zhaun Stribling Hyped by Brock Purdy amid Preseason Success, Fantasy Football Buzz
articles.summary: San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy has been impressed with rookie wide receiver De'Zhaun Stribling throughout the opening weeks of training camp.
articles.body:
San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy has been impressed with rookie wide receiver De'Zhaun Stribling throughout the opening weeks of training camp.

"Obviously really excited about him," Purdy said during a Friday appearance on the Pat McAfee Show (0:25 mark). "He's a smart kid. He's come in, learned our offense. He's got strong hands, great route runner, all the reasons why we drafted him. He's shown it and proven it. Just having him in there with a guy like Mike, Deebo, Demarcus Robinson, we've got a great room of receivers. For him to be able to learn from them but also be able to go out and show that he's willing to be in that starting rotation. He has shown that at camp. We're all really excited about him."

Fantasy Football Sleepers Getting Buzz 🐝

Predicting When Injured Stars Will Debut

The 49ers selected Stribling in the second round of the 2026 NFL draft, adding him with the No. 33 overall pick.

He wrapped up an encouraging performance during San Francisco's 41-17 preseason victory over the Los Angeles Chargers on Thursday, catching four of his five targets for 46 yards.

The 23-year-old also hauled in seven receptions for 63 yards during his preseason debut against the Tennessee Titans on Aug. 14.

With Stribling's early production as well as the praise he received from Purdy, it isn't difficult to imagine him immediately becoming a key piece of San Francisco's passing attack. It also makes him an intriguing option for fantasy football managers.

The 49ers will open their 2026 campaign against the Los Angeles Rams on Sept. 10.

articles.title: Drake Maye Ranked 11th-Best NFL Player Under 25 by Coaches & Execs, What Other QBs Made List?
articles.summary: Drake Maye is the best quarterback in the league among players who are under 25 years old, at least in the eyes of NFL coaches and executives.
articles.body:
Drake Maye is the best quarterback in the league among players who are under 25 years old, at least in the eyes of NFL coaches and executives.

Mike Jones of The Athletic shared rankings of players under 25 from coaches and executives around the league Friday, and everyone is looking up at Detroit Lions offensive lineman Penei Sewell.

But in the quarterback department, Maye is ranked highest at No. 11 and ahead of Jayden Daniels (No. 13), C.J. Stroud (No. 19) and Caleb Williams (No. 21).

That Maye is the highest-ranked quarterback isn't that surprising considering he just led the New England Patriots to the Super Bowl and finished second in MVP voting in his second season in the league during the 2025 campaign.

Williams, Daniels and Maye were the first three picks of the 2024 NFL draft in that order, and they have all enjoyed various degrees of success in their first two years. Only Maye has been to the Super Bowl, but Daniels led the Washington Commanders to the NFC Championship Game as a rookie and Williams' Chicago Bears are coming off an NFC North title.

They will be compared to each other throughout the rest of their careers and could end up switching spots on lists like this a number of times moving forward.

And as long as they all continue to play up to their potential and guide their teams to the playoffs, the Patriots, Commanders and Bears will surely be pleased with their franchise quarterbacks no matter which one is ranked ahead of the others on subjective lists.

Perhaps the most notable inclusion is Stroud, who is one of the more intriguing case studies in the NFL at this point.

He wasted no time establishing himself as a star in the league as the Offensive Rookie of the Year in 2023. He also led the Houston Texans to the playoffs in each of his first three years.

However, Stroud failed to replicate his rookie impact in either his second or third year in the league and threw four interceptions in Houston's playoff loss to the Patriots last season. He seems to have taken a step back with more experience, which makes his long-term future a legitimate question.

While he is extension eligible, he and the Texans have not yet agreed to a new deal.

Stroud will have a chance to bounce back in his fourth season, and there may be a new deal and a higher ranking in lists like these waiting for him if he does.

articles.title: Live NFL Preseason Week 2 Fantasy Football Takeaways and Advice from Friday's Games
articles.summary: The second week of the NFL preseason is well underway. It's less than three weeks until the Seattle Seahawks host the New England Patriots in a rematch of Super Bowl LX that marks the official beginning of the 2026 NFL season—and with it, another season of fantasy football.
articles.body:
The preseason is a time of great hope. And great hype.

Broncos running back Jonah Coleman is the source of both right now. Not that long ago, Coleman was just a Day 3 rookie joining a crowded Broncos backfield. But after less than 10 preseason carries, some are already anointing the 5'8", 220-pounder the future in the Denver backfield .

The Broncos have seen something they like—after one series and three carries against the Green Bay Packers, Coleman got the bubble-wrap treatment. And with an ADP in the 12th round, whether the future is now or not doesn't really matter. There's also JK Dobbins' durability issues to consider.

But unless Dobbins (or RJ Harvey) gets hurt, Coleman isn't going to see more than a handful of touches per game. And for all the hoopla, we're talking about a guy with seven carries for 33 yards against backups.

articles.title: Ravens Say They Are Aware of Receiver Rashod Bateman's June Arrest in Georgia Domestic Case
articles.summary: BALTIMORE (AP) — The Baltimore Ravens said Friday they are aware of Rashod Bateman's arrest in June in Georgia over a domestic violence incident and have been in contact with their receiver.
articles.body:
BALTIMORE (AP) — The Baltimore Ravens said Friday they are aware of Rashod Bateman's arrest in June in Georgia over a domestic violence incident and have been in contact with their receiver.

The Ravens have informed the NFL, and league spokesman Brian McCarthy says the case is under review.

"We notified the league office and have been cooperating throughout the process," the team said in a statement. "As this is a pending legal matter, we will not have further comment."

According to TMZ, Bateman was arrested after smashing a window of the vehicle being driven by the mother of his child, with the 3-month-old inside. TMZ cited court documents that said the victim told authorities the incident happened around 6 a.m. on June 6.

According to the arrest warrant, Bateman used an object to smash the driver's side window, and the shattered glass caused multiple small lacerations to the victim's face.

Bateman's representatives said the receiver turned himself in to the Walton County sheriff's office the same day. A court later granted Bateman's request to lift a no-contact order after he said the victim indicated she did want to have contact with him.

"It is unfortunate that a personal family situation has been taken completely out of context for sensational reasons," Bateman attorney Jordan Siev said in a statement to The Associated Press. "We will let the court process play out and the facts will come out at that time."

Walton County authorities didn't immediately respond to a message from the AP.

Last year, Bateman signed a $37 million, three-year contract extension coming off career bests of 756 yards and nine touchdowns receiving in 2024. The 26-year-old Georgia native who played in college at Minnesota dropped off to a career-low 224 yards with two TDs last season.

articles.title: Jets Record 2 INTs vs. Steelers After Making NFL History with Zero Picks During 2025-26 Season
articles.summary: The New York Jets defense had more success picking off passes in one preseason game than they did all of last season.
articles.body:
The New York Jets defense had more success picking off passes in one preseason game than they did all of last season.

The Jets picked off the Pittsburgh Steelers twice during Friday night's preseason action after becoming the first team since at least 1933 to go a full season without an interception.

The picks were thrown by Steelers quarterback Will Howard on back-to-back drives during the second quarter.

The first interception came at the Jets' 14-yard line, when Howard tried to find Roman Wilson on a short pass that was picked off by the Jets' Andre Cisco.

On the following drive at the Jets' 37-yard line, Howard again tried to find Wilson for a short pass and was picked off by Samuel Womack.

It's been almost exactly a year since the Jets last recorded an interception when Malachi Moore picked off an overthrown pass from Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Kyle McCord on Aug. 22, 2025.

Jets cornerback Nahshon Wright said earlier this offseason he didn't think the team's lack of interceptions last season had been brought up in meetings, per NyJets.com's Jack Bell .

"I think 2025 was 2025 and I think we're trying to turn over a new leaf, so we haven't spoken about it at all," Wright said, per Bell.

The Jets will now hope to build on Friday's defensive performance when opening the regular season Sept. 13 against the Tennessee Titans.

articles.title: Nick Chubb Announces NFL Retirement, 4-Time Pro Bowler Played 8 Seasons for Browns, Texans
articles.summary: Four-time Pro Bowl running back Nick Chubb announced his retirement from the NFL at 30 years old in an Instagram post on Friday.
articles.body:
Four-time Pro Bowl running back Nick Chubb announced his retirement from the NFL at 30 years old in an Instagram post on Friday.

"Football was a huge blessing in my life," Chubb wrote as part of the announcement. "It opened so many doors, gave me opportunities I never could have imagined, and allowed me to meet some amazing people. I'm grateful for everyone I crossed paths with along the way, and I promise I took something from each of you. Thank you to my teammates, my coaches, the fans, my family, my friends, and anyone who ever cheered me on. Twelve year old me could have never imagined where this game would take us. But 30 year old me can look back and say we gave it everything we had."

Chubb spent seven seasons with the Cleveland Browns and one year with the Houston Texans after coming back from a knee injury that ended his 2023 campaign and required multiple surgeries.

The former Georgia standout was initially selected by the Browns with a second-round pick in the 2018 NFL draft.

Chubb immediately became a crucial piece of Cleveland's offense, rushing for 996 yards and eight touchdowns as a rookie before going on to earn Pro Bowl nods in each of the next four years.

This included a 2022 season in which he amassed 1,525 yards on the ground, ranking No. 3 among all players.

Chubb only appeared in two games during his 2023 campaign before tearing his left MCL and sustaining damage to his meniscus and medial capsule. It represented his second significant knee injury, as he previously suffered a torn MCL, PCL and LCL in the same left knee while playing for Georgia in 2015.

The 2023 injury ended his season and also delayed his 2024 debut until Week 7.

While Chubb returned for Cleveland's 2024 campaign, he missed the final three games of the year due to a broken foot .

He later joined the Houston Texans and appeared in 15 games last year, rushing for 506 yards and three touchdowns.

Chubb averaged 5.2 yards per carry across his five NFL seasons prior to the knee injury, but averaged just 3.7 yards per carry in two years after returning.

Still, he's finishing his career with 7,349 rush yards and 54 touchdowns while sitting at No. 3 on the Browns' all-time rushing leaderboard .

With Week 1 of the 2026 season drawing closer, Chubb is choosing to step away from the sport.

articles.title: Cade Klubnik, Drew Allar, Will Howard's Final Box Score Stats and Highlights from Jets vs. Steelers
articles.summary: A trio of young quarterbacks made their case to earn NFL playing time during Friday night's preseason action between the Pittsburgh Steelers andNew York Jets.
articles.body:
A trio of young quarterbacks made their case to earn NFL playing time during Friday night's preseason action between the Pittsburgh Steelers andNew York Jets.

2026 fourth-round pick Cade Klubnik saw playing time for the Jets while Will Howard (2025 sixth-round pick) and Drew Allar (2026 third-rounder) both played for the Steelers.

Here's a look at how these rookie quarterbacks did during Saturday night action in Pittsburgh.

Klubnik scrambled for 16 yards on 3rd and two in the first quarter, although the drive ended in a punt for the Jets.

He also took two sacks and a grounding penalty before closing out the night with no scoring drives on five possessions.

Howard made his first start Saturday since leading Ohio State to a national title over Notre Dame in January 2025.

After his first two drives ended in punts, Howard struggled in the second quarter by throwing back-to-back interceptions for the Steelers.

The Jets had recorded zero interceptions throughout the entirety of the 2025 season before pulling down two from Howard.

Allar stepped in to lead the Steelers in the second half. He made a 38-yard completion to Lake McRee in the third quarter.

The offensive line struggled to protect Allar down the stretch as he took three sacks before closing out the loss. Steelers wide receivers also dropped multiple potential completions from the quarterback.

Klubnik is currently slated to back up Jets starter Geno Smith, while the Steelers need to decide which quarterbacks to keep behind Aaron Rodgers out of Howard, Allar and Mason Howard.

Howard and Allar will get one last chance to compete for their roster spots during next Thursday's preseason finale at the Buffalo Bills. Klubnik could next see action when the Jets wrap up their own preseason slate Friday against the New York Giants.

articles.title: New Fantasy Football 2026 Dynasty Draft Rankings, Keeper Advice and Team Names
articles.summary: The second week of the NFL preseason is underway, which means that we have officially entered fantasy draft season. While most fantasy enthusiasts will engage in traditional redraft leagues in the coming weeks, many diehards will dive into dynasty and keeper formats.
articles.body:
The second week of the NFL preseason is underway, which means that we have officially entered fantasy draft season. While most fantasy enthusiasts will engage in traditional redraft leagues in the coming weeks, many diehards will dive into dynasty and keeper formats.

Playing in a dynasty league—and to a lesser extent, a keeper league—requires a strong commitment. However, there's a level of satisfaction that comes with building a multi-year contender that redraft leagues and daily fantasy sports cannot provide.

While the goals of a dynasty draft are a little different than a typical fantasy draft—you'll want to focus heavily on younger long-term options—that's where things start. Here, you'll find a look at some updated 2026 dynasty draft rankings, along with a few other resources for dynasty and keeper play.

Jaxon Smith-Njigba, WR, Seattle Seahawks

Omarion Hampton, RB, Los Angeles Chargers

Christian McCaffrey, RB, San Francisco 49ers

If you're at all familiar with dynasty formats, you already know that they involve a multi-year approach. So do traditional keeper leagues, though recovering from a bad season isn't nearly as difficult.

In keeper leagues, having two keeper slots is pretty standard. This means that managers can keep up to two of their best players and redraft the rest.

In dynasty leagues, rebuilding isn't as straightforward. As is the case in the real NFL, the goal is to draft players who will contribute for many years. OF course, this includes the risk of getting stuck with bad players for several seasons, too.

The best way to rebuild in dynasty leagues is through yearly rookie drafts. However, any manager hoping to add a promising rookie like quarterback Fernando Mendoza , running back Jeremiyah Love , or wide receiver Carnell Tate will have to make room by first dumping veterans from their roster.

Obviously, it's preferable to part with underperforming players in order to make room for rookie talent. Contenders with strong overall rosters, however, will find the process more challenging.

Dynasty managers will want to keep younger centerpiece players such as wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase, quarterback Josh Allen, running back Bijan Robinson, and tight end Brock Bowers. Elite players firmly in their prime playing windows should always earn a spot on your roster.

When evaluating non-quarterbacks, lean toward players under the age of 30.

Keeping older players can still make sense for managers in their championship window. However, anyone rostering, say, 36-year-old tight end Travis Kelce will want to have long-term insurance at the position. Pairing Kelce with a rookie tight end like Kenyon Sadiq would be a great approach in this scenario.

If forced to choose between high-level skill players, it's typically best to favor wide receivers and tight ends over running backs. An every-down back will usually provide the better season-long floor, but backs tend to have shorter careers than their pass-catching counterparts—though aging stars like Christian McCaffrey and Derrick Henry are bucking the trend.

The rules in keeper leagues are a bit different since you're only keeping players for another season—and, again, usually two at most. The general rule is to keep players who will provide greater value than your draft slot.

If, for example, you see McCaffrey trending as a fifth or sixth overall pick, and you're picking 11th, keeping the 30-year-old for another season would make perfect sense. Ideally, you'll be able to keep two first-round talents while making your first redraft selection in Round 3.

Of course, it's difficult to know which top-tier players will be available to redraft unless your league makes keeper picks public. There will be some guesswork involved here, and you'll have to weigh the value of your top players against those you expect to be available.

Managers can generally expect top performers like Robinson, Chase, Jahmyr Gibbs, and Jaxon Smith-Njigba to not reenter the draft pool in keeper leagues, however.

Tetairoa McMillan, WR, Carolina Panthers

Kenneth Walker III, RB, Kansas City Chiefs

Jayden Daniels, QB, Washington Commanders

League Goes On, And On, And On, And On, And On

articles.title: When Shedeur Sanders vs. Deshaun Watson QB1 Battle Will Be Decided Revealed in New Browns Rumors
articles.summary: As Shedeur Sanders prepares to make his first preseason start on Saturday against the Buffalo Bills, the Cleveland Browns could name their Week 1 starting quarterback not long after.
articles.body:
As Shedeur Sanders prepares to make his first preseason start on Saturday against the Buffalo Bills, the Cleveland Browns could name their Week 1 starting quarterback not long after.

Appearing on the Saturday morning SportsCenter , ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported Browns head coach Todd Monken could make a decision between Sanders and Deshaun Watson as soon as Monday:

"Shedeur Sanders will get the first half today. I'm told this quarterback battle is still in full swing, even though Deshaun Watson, the veteran, has had some momentum in the last few weeks. What Shedeur does today is a major data point in the process. He won't have all the starters with him, but he will have a few guys with the first-team offense going at it. And I'm told this is how it's going to go; head coach Todd Monken will get through today, he'll get with his staff on Sunday, he'll evaluate all the tape the last few weeks, he'll get input from his staff. I suspect by Monday they should be ready to make a decision on this quarterback battle."

Shedeur's Reaction to Browns' QB Decision

Watson got the start in Cleveland's preseason opener against the Chicago Bears on Aug. 15. He finished 11-of-15 for 126 yards, lost a fumble and led the Browns to 10 points on six drives in the first half.

Sanders came on to start the third quarter and played three drives. He went 6-of-11 for 79 yards with one interception. The Browns went scoreless in the second half with Sanders and Dillon Gabriel running the offense.

Monken has been clear throughout training camp and into preseason that there's not much separating the two quarterbacks. He said on the heels of the Bears game it would be "unfair" not to give Sanders an opportunity to play with at least some of the starters in a game before making a decision:

"Again, I did feel going into last game that it was relatively close in terms of both having an opportunity at the starting position, so it would be unfair to not go into the next game and give Shedeur that same opportunity. Albeit a different team, certainly at home. There's no guarantee the same players will be playing in this game, but it's the closest you have, and we owe it to both players who have handled it well and competed at a high level."

Watson's start against the Bears marked his first appearance in a game since Oct. 20, 2024. He tore his right Achilles two different times, including in January 2025 while rehabbing the original injury.

Sanders started the final seven games for the Browns last season. He threw for 1,400 yards, seven touchdowns and 10 interceptions in eight appearances as a rookie.

The Browns do have another preseason game after Saturday when they take on the New England Patriots on Aug. 27, but typically teams won't feature many starters in the last game before the regular season.

Given the quick turnaround for that game, as well, it makes sense the Browns coaches would likely want to settle on their starting quarterback sooner than later so they can begin preparing for Week 1 against the Jacksonville Jaguars on Sept. 13.

articles.title: Eagles' 'Bumpy Road' Explained in New NFL Rumors and Latest Fantasy Outlook on Jalen Hurts, Saquon
articles.summary: Expectations are high for Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts and running back Saquon Barkley under new offensive coordinator Sean Mannion, though there have been some growing pains during training camp.
articles.body:
Expectations are high for Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts and running back Saquon Barkley under new offensive coordinator Sean Mannion, though there have been some growing pains during training camp.

"They're really happy with how open he's been to the changes, taking under-center work, play action, ball fakes, all that stuff," ESPN's Jeremy Fowler said on Saturday's SportsCenter regarding Hurts. "He's really taken to the footwork part of it; got to work early in the offseason. He and Sean Mannion have hit it off in that way. Now, they had a joint practice with the Patriots for two days. The sentiment was it was a little up and down; first day was a little bit rough. That was to be expected because a lot of the receivers had been out. De'Vonta Smith had a hamstring issue, missed multiple weeks. First-round pick Makai Lemon, hamstring, missed multiple weeks. They're finally getting healthy and back into the swing. Hurts doesn't really play in preseason games, so it's expected to be a bit of a bumpy road as they get the offense in full swing. They're hoping by Week 1 they're full strength and then the running game is going to be big. The sentiment there is that with Saquon Barkley getting back to those 20-, 30-yard runs, that will set the stage for Hurts to have a big year."

The Eagles had their share of struggles on offense last season, as the play-calling of offensive coordinator Kevin Patullo and head coach Nick Sirianni often became predictable and stale.

But Hurts also had an up-and-down season, throwing for 3,224 yards, 25 touchdowns and six interceptions while completing 64.8 percent of his passes, taking 32 sacks and rushing for 421 yards and eight touchdowns. The numbers were fine, but Hurts and the Eagles left a lot of meat on the bone in the passing game.

In addition, a once-dominant offensive line battled through a number of injuries and was less ineffective than seasons past. Barkley was pressing, often finding himself trying to make a defender miss before even reaching the line of scrimmage. Wideout A.J. Brown spent much of the season unhappy with the state of the passing game and offense, and wasn't particularly shy in letting those feelings be known publicly.

The result was an offense that ranked 24th in total yards (311.2 YPG), 23rd in passing (194.3 YPG) and 19th in scoring (22.3 PPG). The Eagles still made the playoffs but lost to the San Francisco 49ers in the Wild Card Round.

Major changes followed, with Mannion replacing Patullo. The hope is that his scheme—which will rely more on pre-snap motion, under-center plays and working the middle of the field in the passing game—will revitalize both Hurts and the rest of the offense. So far, the transition has shown real promise.

Hurts is always a viable option in fantasy, given his rushing touchdowns, but a more productive year through the air would give him the potential to be a top-three option at the position. That's the best-case scenario, however, especially with Hurts adjusting to life without Brown. But realistically, Hurts is still a safe starter on a weekly basis.

As for Barkley, a major bounceback season could be brewing, especially if the offensive line is healthy. Don't expect another 2,000-yard season on the ground, but it wouldn't be shocking if he's a top-five running back this season.

articles.title: New NFL Rumors on Bo Nix's Arm Strength and Jaylen Waddle, Updated Fantasy Outlook for Broncos Stars
articles.summary: The addition of wide receiver Jaylen Waddle—and Bo Nix's offseason work to increase his throwing power—has optimism high around the Denver Broncos this summer.
articles.body:
The addition of wide receiver Jaylen Waddle—and Bo Nix's offseason work to increase his throwing power—has optimism high around the Denver Broncos this summer.

"They feel like [Waddle] is the missing piece," ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported on Saturday's SportsCenter . "When you talk to people in Denver, they cannot contain their excitement for Waddle because of how he fits the offense with head coach Sean Payton, new offensive coordinator Davis Webb and Nix. They feel he can work the middle of the field with his route running, but he can also get the yards after the catch, which you see right there. He can get the big play; he can do a little bit of everything. So, the good news with that is, Nix is not only healthy, but they feel like he's added a little layer of arm strength this offseason. He's been really zipping the ball. So, it's a good marriage right now between those two. Everybody's healthy and happy."

Nix has been a nice option for fantasy players in the past two seasons, and having another weapon like Waddle should help him potentially take another jump. He threw for 3,931 yards, 25 touchdowns and 11 interceptions last season, adding 356 yards and five scores on the ground.

Waddle's speed should add another dimension to Denver's passing game, meanwhile. The veteran wideout exceeded 1,000 receiving yards in each of his first three seasons, though he failed to reach that benchmark in each of the past two campaigns as Miami's offense struggled.

But the duo of Waddle and Courtland Sutton—alongside Pat Bryant, Marvin Mims Jr. and Troy Franklin—gives the Broncos a fantastic receiving corps. The Broncos should scheme Waddle plenty of touches, and a return to 1,000 receiving yards—and perhaps something close to the career-high 104 receptions he had as a rookie in 2021—could be on the table. If Waddle hits those benchmarks, he could be a WR2 for fantasy players this season.

As it stands, he's probably best served being drafted as more of a high-end flex option, while Nix is a low-end QB1. But both could be excellent values in the middle rounds at your upcoming fantasy drafts.

articles.title: Bills GM Brandon Beane Releases Statement on Death of Ed Oliver's Son
articles.summary: The Buffalo Bills announced Saturday that defensive lineman Ed Oliver is grieving the death of his son.
articles.body:
The Buffalo Bills announced Saturday that defensive lineman Ed Oliver is grieving the death of his son.

Bills general manager Brandon Beane released a statement on the matter, writing, "On behalf of the entire Buffalo Bills organization, we want to publicly express our condolences to Ed Oliver and his family on the devastating loss of his son. It's an unthinkable tragedy for any parent. We will continue to support Ed and his family as we all grieve this tragic loss."

Predicting When Injured Stars Will Debut

Oliver's son was two years old at the time of his death, according to Lance Lysowski and Stephen T. Watson of the Buffalo News .

Oliver, 28, has spent his entire seven-year NFL career with the Bills after the team selected him ninth overall in the 2019 draft out of the University of Houston.

Over seven campaigns and 95 regular-season games with the Bills, he has recorded 30 sacks and 56 tackles for loss.

Ankle and biceps injuries limited Oliver to just three games last season, but he is expected to be a significant part of new defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard's defense in 2026.

articles.title: Geno Smith 'Throwing The Mess Out of the Ball,' Says Jets Insider and New Rumors on Cade Klubnik
articles.summary: While Geno Smith impressed for the New York Jets during Friday night's preseason matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers, more clarity is emerging regarding the battle for the backup gig.
articles.body:
While Geno Smith impressed for the New York Jets during Friday night's preseason matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers, more clarity is emerging regarding the battle for the backup gig.

"They're still working that out. Cade Klubnik, the early Day 3 draft pick, has been growing in profile behind the scenes in recent weeks. They are high on him," ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported during Saturday's SportsCenter . "Now, he was accurate last night, but he didn't score any points on his several drives. So, it was a situation where he could've taken the reins on that QB2 job, didn't quite do it yet. But it appears that he should be able to beat out Brady Cook and Bailey Zappe, the veteran. So, they like what they see, and he'll be on the roster regardless, most likely, but he's vying for that QB2 job. The signs are good so far, just didn't put up any points last night. Smith has been throwing 'the mess' out of the ball. That's the phrase that was used behind the scenes from people with the Jets. They're really excited."

Smith looked impressive in his first preseason action on Friday, finishing 7-of-7 for 65 yards and a touchdown. New York improved the offense around him in the offseason, drafting wideout Omar Cooper Jr. and tight end Kenyon Sadiq in the first round, and the early signs against the Steelers were promising.

"Very, very efficient," Jets coach Aaron Glenn told reporters after the game. "He threw to five different receivers, he looked really comfortable. It was exactly what we were looking for."

Meanwhile, Klubnik finished 10-of-14 for 75 yards, though he didn't lead the Jets on any scoring drives. Still, the fourth-round pick appears to be in the driver's seat to win the backup gig.

articles.title: J.J. McCarthy's Final Box Score Stats and Highlights from Vikings vs. Ravens
articles.summary: J.J. McCarthy failed to lead the Minnesota Vikings on a scoring drive during his four drives on the field on Saturday against the Baltimore Ravens.
articles.body:
J.J. McCarthy failed to lead the Minnesota Vikings on a scoring drive during his four drives on the field on Saturday against the Baltimore Ravens.

McCarthy had a few nice moments, but his inability to finish off a drive in the red zone stood out the most.

None of the Vikings quarterbacks led them to the end zone, though, as the Ravens won 13-3.

McCarthy's highlight reel play came in the first quarter on a 50-yard pass to Tai Felton.

Unfortunately for McCarthy and the Vikings, that was the most notable play on their second drive of the game.

McCarthy had a few opportunities to hit open receivers in the red zone, but he failed to connect on second down with Felton and on fourth down with Myles Price.

McCarthy only picked up 31 yards on his other four completions. He faced a ton of pressure over his four drives from the Ravens pass rush.

Minnesota was forced to punt on three of the four McCarthy-led drives. The other fizzled out with a turnover on downs at the goal line.

McCarthy had one series in the second quarter before he was replaced by Carson Wentz.

McCarthy's final audition to confirm his role as the team's backup quarterback comes on Friday against the Denver Broncos.

articles.title: Fantasy Football 2026 Rookie Sleepers Undervalued in Drafts
articles.summary: Some of the most sought-after targets in fantasy football were among the most prominent picks at the 2026 NFL Draft.
articles.body:
Some of the most sought-after targets in fantasy football were among the most prominent picks at the 2026 NFL Draft.

Prized rookie rookie running back Jeremiyah Love is often gone by the end of Round 2, while receiver Carnell Tate is typically snatched by Round 6.

The appeal is obvious with both. Given the draft capital invested in them by the Arizona Cardinals and Tennessee Titans, respectively, they will be given every chance to succeed and could have mammoth workloads right away.

These aren't, of course, the only fantasy-relevant rookies we'll see. The reasons might be less obvious, but the following three players all have opportunities to deliver impact production at a bargain draft price.

By trade, KC Concepcion is an NFL wideout. By practice, he's more of a makes-things-happen playmaker.

Over a three-year college career split between NC State and Texas A&M, Concepcion made noise (and put up numbers) as a pass-catcher, ball-carrier and punt returner. During his preseason debut, it was more of the same, as he tallied three catches (on four targets) for 27 yards, a 14-yard touchdown run and a 31-yard punt return.

That versatility definitely helps. It gives him a chance to be more involved, for one, but it also could allow him to make an impact without being entirely dependent on this passing attack, which feels enormously helpful given the state of Cleveland's quarterback room.

He has a dynamic burst, open-field shiftiness and a knack for sniffing out the best path to a big play. He would, admittedly, be even more interesting in a more functional offense, but he'd also probably cost a lot more in a fantasy draft, then.

Little is known and even less is proven about the revamped passing game in Miami. New quarterback Malik Willis has made six career starts in four seasons. Starting receivers Jalen Tolbert and Malik Washington have yet to clear 620 receiving yards in a season.

That, admittedly, makes any investment into this aerial attack a true blind leap of faith. That said, it also allows just about anyone to fast-track their way into a prominent role, and it sure sounds like third-round rookie Caleb Douglas is doing exactly that. He snagged a starting spot on the team's first depth chart, then promptly posted what will be one of the best catches we'll see all season.

"He's making plays left and right," veteran tight end Greg Dulcich told reporters . "It's awesome. He's showing up all over the field."

Douglas looks the part of an impact receiver. He has size, a big catch radius, physicality and an intriguing mix of quickness and speed. He had tantalizing moments in college, but it often felt like he was capable of so much more if he ever put it all together. If that's what's happening right now, he could be a real find in fantasy.

De'Zhaun Stribling, WR, San Francisco 49ers

While it has been a stock-up preseason so far for the second-round pick, De'Zhaun Stribling still offers significant sleeper appeal.

He could be hard-charging his way toward a prominent role in what should be one of the league's most potent offenses. The 49ers have other playmakers on paper, sure, but they just about all come attached to age and injury concerns. If Stribling simply looks solid, he'd at least be positioned for some by-default duties in place of an injured veteran.

But he looks like he might be a lot more than that. He's had 13 passes thrown his way this preseason and converted those chances into 11 receptions for 109 yards. He runs crisp routes, has great hands, boasts explosive speed (4.36-second 40-yard dash at the Combine) and blocks the way coach Kyle Shanahan demands his receivers to.

At this rate, it feels like Stribling has a navigable path to WR2 duties for the 49ers with if-everything-breaks-right WR1 upside.

articles.title: Bears Donate $200K to Support Illinois, Indiana Communities Affected by Severe Storms
articles.summary: The Chicago Bears announced Saturday that they are donating $200,000 to aid in recovery from severe storms and flooding that impacted the southern suburbs of Chicago and Northwest Indiana.
articles.body:
The Chicago Bears announced Saturday that they are donating $200,000 to aid in recovery from severe storms and flooding that impacted the southern suburbs of Chicago and Northwest Indiana.

Donations will be split evenly with $100,000 going to Catholic Charities of the Archdiocese of Chicago and $100,000 being provided to Catholic Charities of the Diocese of Gary.

The Bears noted that both organizations are "helping address immediate and ongoing needs in affected communities, including food, clothing, housing assistance and other recovery resources where many families remain without power, displaced from their homes and face a long rebuilding process."

According to ABC7 in Chicago, at least seven storm-related deaths were reported, and nearly 150,000 customers were still without power in Northwest Indiana as of last Sunday.

Buffalo Bills defensive back Damar Hamlin intercepted Cleveland Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders on Saturday, and he had some fun at his expense by hitting the watch flex while celebrating with his teammates.

articles.title: Anthony Richardson, Top Players' Final Box Score Stats and Highlights from Falcons vs. Colts
articles.summary: Anthony Richardson didn't do himself any favors in his battle for the Indianapolis Colts' backup quarterback job during the team's 34-6 preseason loss to the Atlanta Falcons at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis on Saturday.
articles.body:
Anthony Richardson didn't do himself any favors in his battle for the Indianapolis Colts' backup quarterback job during the team's 34-6 preseason loss to the Atlanta Falcons at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis on Saturday.

Despite entering the game as 3.5-point favorites, according to FanDuel , the Colts faltered out of the gate and were outscored 24-6 in the first half.

Here is a look at the stat lines for Richardson and other notable contributors from the second game of the preseason for both Indianapolis and Atlanta:

With starting quarterback Daniel Jones sitting, Colts head coach Shane Steichen decided to give Riley Leonard and Richardson one half each in order to stake their claim to the QB2 spot.

After getting the start, Leonard struggled to get much going on offense during the first half, going just 7-of-14 for 62 yards with no touchdowns or interceptions. He then gave way to Richardson, who played the entire second half.

The offense didn't look any better with Richardson at the helm, as the No. 4 overall pick in the 2023 NFL draft went just 3-of-9 for 24 yards with no touchdowns or interceptions through the air, while also rushing for 15 yards on three carries.

Neither Tua Tagovailoa nor Michael Penix Jr. saw action at quarterback for the Falcons, but their offense ran far more smoothly than Indy's nonetheless.

Even with star skill-position players in running back Bijan Robinson, wide receiver Drake London and tight end Kyle Pitts all sitting, both Cooper Rush and Jack Strand impressed under center for Atlanta.

Rush got the start and played most of the first half, going 10-of-11 for 86 yards with no touchdowns or interceptions.

Strand took over late in the first half and played the entire second half, going 12-of-17 for 212 yards with one touchdown and no interceptions. He also rushed for 22 yards and a score on nine totes.

An undrafted rookie out of Division II Minnesota State-Moorhead, Strand has been a revelation for the Falcons so far this preseason.

After Tagovailoa and Rush both played poorly in the Falcons' 27-7 loss to the Denver Broncos in their preseason opener, Strand was responsible for Atlanta's only points, as he rushed for a one-yard touchdown.

It is unclear how many quarterbacks the Falcons intend to keep on their 53-man roster, but Strand has seemingly put himself firmly in the mix to be either the QB3 or the backup if Penix is not fully recovered from the torn ACL he suffered last season once the 2026 regular season starts.

As for the Colts, Jones appears locked in as the starter despite coming back from a torn Achilles, but neither Richardson nor Leonard have firmly established themselves as the clear backup.

Both the Falcons and Colts will wrap up their preseason schedules next week when Atlanta faces the Miami Dolphins on Friday and Indianapolis faces the Detroit Lions on Saturday.

articles.title: Michael Penix Jr. Takes Big Step in Knee Injury Rehab amid Falcons QB1 Battle with Tua
articles.summary: Atlanta Falcons quarterback and potential starter Michael Penix Jr. has taken a step forward in his recovery from knee surgery.
articles.body:
Atlanta Falcons quarterback and potential starter Michael Penix Jr. has taken a step forward in his recovery from knee surgery.

Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski said Saturday Penix has been cleared for 11-on-11 practice.

When asked how the Falcons planned to ramp Penix up to game speed, Stefanski said, "He'll practice Monday in team periods."

Penix has previously been limited to quarterback drills and seven-on-seven practice while rehabbing from the torn ACL he suffered last November.

Stefanski has yet to announce whether Penix or Tua Tagovailoa will be starting when the Falcons kick off the regular season Sept. 13 at the Pittsburgh Steelers.

Penix tore his left ACL while playing against the Carolina Panthers on Nov. 16 and underwent surgery later that month.

That marked the third ACL repair surgery for Penix, who recovered from two torn right ACLs while playing for Indiana.

Penix told reporters last week recovery from his latest injury was not just a physical but also a mental process of learning to trust his knee again.

"If something bad happened to you, and you remember every step that took up to that place that something bad happened to you, the next time you're going to do it, you're going to think about it again... it's like, okay, yes, I am healthy, but do I trust that?" Penix said last week.

Getting Penix back on the field for full team drills could be key to the team naming a QB1, which Stefanski declined to do when announcing Tagovailoa would start the team's preseason opener.

Tagovailoa played two drives in that preseason opener and did not see action in the Falcons' Saturday matchup as Cooper Rush and Jack Strand played against the Indianapolis Colts.

Quarterbacks coach Alex Van Pelt said last week he felt Penix had "done everything he could possibly do to put himself in position to compete" for the QB1 position despite missing out on full team drills.

"We'll reset and kind of take a look at it from the big picture once he's available," Van Pelt said about the quarterback competition.

Depending on how Penix's participation in practice goes this week, the Falcons could potentially have all four of their quarterbacks available when wrapping up the preseason Friday against Tagovalioa's former teammates on the Miami Dolphins.

articles.title: Shedeur Sanders, Deshaun Watson's Final Box Score Stats and Highlights from Browns vs. Bills
articles.summary: Shedeur Sanders, Deshaun Watson and the Cleveland Browns struggled against Kyle Allen and the Buffalo Bills in preseason action, falling 31-7 as the duo combined for just 109 yards and two interceptions.
articles.body:
Shedeur Sanders, Deshaun Watson and the Cleveland Browns struggled against Kyle Allen and the Buffalo Bills in preseason action, falling 31-7 as the duo combined for just 109 yards and two interceptions.

The Browns were 1.5-point underdogs, according to FanDuel Sportsbook , and lived up to their billing as such after both potential starters struggled to find their footing Saturday in Cleveland.

Sanders got the start and played through the first half before veteran Watson took over after halftime, a reversal of last week's sequencing. Former Oregon standout Dillon Gabriel then stepped in to close out the game in the fourth quarter.

After Buffalo opened the game with a score, the Browns responded with an 11-play drive that ended with an 8-yard touchdown pass from Sanders to Luke Floriea to even the score at seven.

After three straight punts, Sanders threw a pass behind his intended receiver that was picked off by Damar Hamlin. The Bills added another score before the end of the half to take a 14-7 lead into halftime.

Watson took over for the Browns in a scoreless third quarter for the team, struggling out of the gate, gaining negative-one yard on three plays before punting on the ensuing possession. The vet then threw an interception under pressure with just over three minutes remaining in the frame that set up the Bills' third touchdown of the game.

Gabriel took over late in the fourth quarter after Watson and the Browns turned the ball over on downs as the Bills put the finishing touches on a dominant win.

Last season, the Browns finished last in the AFC North at 5-12 after playing both Sanders, who appeared in eight games and threw for 1,400 yards and seven touchdowns, and Gabriel, who threw for 937 yards and seven touchdowns over 10 games, at quarterback.

This season, with Watson returning from injury, the competition is on once again, but it has shifted between the 10th-year veteran and the second-year player.

In the Browns' preseason opener, they dropped a 34-10 loss to the Chicago Bears as they began their experimental run while determining who will be under center come Week 1.

Head coach Todd Monken has yet to name a starter, while last week, Watson got the nod in the first half, completing 11-of-15 passes for 126 yards with one sack, while Sanders took over after halftime.

The former Colorado standout threw for 79 yards on 6-of-11 passing with one interception before Gabriel took over.

Cleveland will close out its preseason Thursday against the New England Patriots at home.
